shower.thought: We measure how much we've grown by comparing ourselves to who we used to be, but we never actually know who we'll become, so growth might just be the act of surprising yourself.
The people closest to you know your flaws better than anyone, yet they're the ones most likely to defend you anyway—that's probably what love actually is.
You can't remember most of your life, which means you're basically a different person with someone else's memories.
Nostalgia is just your brain editing out all the parts that were actually boring or painful and keeping only the highlights—so your best memories might be fiction.
We say "I need to find myself" but we spend most of our time running away from what we'd actually find.
The only time you truly have nothing to lose is when you haven't admitted to yourself yet that you were losing.
Your embarrassing memories will eventually embarrass you so much that they become endearing—time doesn't heal wounds, it just recontextualizes them.
If you had to bet your life on it, you probably couldn't prove most of what you believe is true, yet you organize your entire existence around these unprovable things.
Silence between friends and silence between strangers feel completely different, but they're literally the same thing—it's just what you've already shared that changes the sound.
We're terrified of being forgotten, but being remembered for the wrong reasons might actually be worse than disappearing completely.
The moment you become self-aware about your own patterns is the moment you're stuck between knowing better and being who you are.
You only realize how much you were struggling when you finally stop—which means most of your suffering is invisible, even to you.
Happiness might just be the absence of comparing yourself to others, which is why it's so hard to find in a world built on comparison.
We teach kids not to touch hot stoves, but we never teach them how to know which people are hot stoves disguised as warm hugs.
Your conscience is just peer pressure from yourself—a version of you that you've internalized so completely that you forgot it was constructed.
The reason we fear death so much might be that we're already spending most of our lives not fully alive, so we're not sure what we'd actually be losing.
You can't unhear a song once it's in your head, can't unsee something once you've noticed it, can't unknow something once you've learned it—so every experience is permanent, even the small ones.
The things you say you'll do "someday" are usually the things you've already decided not to do, but you're not honest enough to admit it yet.
Admitting you were wrong requires believing that your current self is better than your past self, which is optimism disguised as accountability.
We spend decades learning how to survive in a world, and then we spend the rest of our lives unlearning all of it to actually enjoy it.

motivational.thought:
Everything you want is on the other side of fear. The only question is whether you're willing to walk through it.
— Unknown

The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago. The second best time is now.
— Ancient Proverb

You are not obligated to become the person others thought you'd be.
— Unknown

Success is not final and failure is not fatal. It's the courage to continue that counts.
— Winston Churchill

The person you're becoming will be grateful for the choices you're making right now.
— Unknown

Don't wait for permission to be yourself. It was never anyone's to give.
— Unknown

Small progress is still progress. Keep moving.
— Unknown

You don't rise to the level of your goals; you fall to the level of your systems. Build better ones.
— Unknown

The regret of not trying will always hurt more than the pain of failing.
— Unknown

What would you attempt if you knew you couldn't fail?
— Robert H. Schuller

Your life is not a dress rehearsal. Stop treating it like one.
— Unknown

Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most.
— Unknown

The obstacle is the way. What blocks your path becomes the path.
— Marcus Aurelius

You don't need to see the whole staircase to take the first step.
— Martin Luther King Jr.

Everything difficult was once impossible. You're closer than you think.
— Unknown

Stop waiting for the right moment. Any moment you decide to act is the right one.
— Unknown

Your struggle today is building the strength you'll need tomorrow.
— Unknown

The only guarantee in life is that things will change. Make sure you're changing too.
— Unknown

Bold action beats perfect planning. You learn by doing, not thinking.
— Unknown

Comparison is the thief of joy, and mediocrity is the thief of potential.
— Unknown

darkjoke.thought:
I told my wife she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My grandfather said, "Your generation is too reliant on technology."
I said, "You're right," and unplugged his life support.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

My friend said he wanted to die doing what he loved.
I said, "Procrastinating?"
He said, "No, disappointing people."

I asked the funeral director if he ever gets tired of his job.
He said, "Not really. Business is dying."

My therapist told me to think positive.
I said, "Okay, I'm positive you're overcharging me."

I told my kid the tooth fairy wasn't real.
He said, "I know, Mom."
I said, "Then who's been leaving money under your pillow?"
He said, "That's the weird part."

My doctor said I needed to cut back on drinking.
I said, "Okay," and switched to a smaller glass.
I used to be addicted to soap, but I'm clean now.

My friend asked me to help him move a dead body.
I said, "Absolutely not."
He said, "Come on, we go way back."
I said, "Exactly. I remember what happened last time."

People keep asking how I stay so calm.
Honestly, it's the medication. Without it, I'm furious at everyone, including myself.

I went to a self-help seminar on overcoming anxiety.
I left after ten minutes.
The speaker kept making eye contact.

My wife asked if I was seeing someone else.
I said, "Yes, but only because you're standing in the way."

I told my son that life isn't fair.
He said, "I know, you won another custody battle."

The doctor said I had six months to live.
I couldn't pay the bill.
He said I had a year.

My friend asked me to be honest about whether his new haircut looked good.
I said, "It's a solid choice if you're going for 'recently divorced dad at a Costco.'"
He said, "Is it that bad?"
I said, "Worse. It's that accurate."

I asked my therapist if I was making progress.
She said, "Absolutely. This is the first session where you didn't mention your childhood trauma."
I said, "I'm saving it for the memoir."
She said, "We can't afford that."

My car broke down, so I called a mechanic.
He said, "The engine's seized."
I said, "Well, it had a good run."
He said, "It's been two weeks."

I told my date I was recently divorced.
She asked, "How long ago?"
I said, "Pending."
She said, "You're still married?"
I said, "No, the paperwork's pending."
She said, "And you're on a date?"
I said, "She hasn't served me yet, so technically I'm single."

My kid asked why I looked so tired all the time.
I said, "Because parenting is exhausting."
He said, "You could just give me up for adoption."
I said, "I'm working on it."
